candidate.title: No rule ties `retain_until` to credential expiry: a reservation evicted before `effective_expiry` reopens replay for the remaining lifetime (refines the iteration-5 retain_until candidate with a single well-formed hunk)
candidate.claim: Refinement of the iteration-5 candidate that was dropped for invalid diff syntax, not for substance. §3.2 makes `retain_until` REQUIRED and says the host MUST retain the nonce until that time, but nothing constrains its value: it may be less than `now_unix`, or less than the credential's `effective_expiry`. Because §9 defines expiry as strict `now_unix >= effective_expiry`, the proof remains acceptable for every second in (retain_until, effective_expiry). A host that honors the spec literally evicts at `retain_until`, after which the identical bundle re-presents with the identical `consume_nonces` and reserves cleanly — replay with no deny signal. Binding v2 signs `expiry` so the presenter cannot move expiry, but the verifier chooses `retain_until` unilaterally and the host has no obligation to sanity-check it. The fix needs two obligations: verifier `retain_until` MUST be >= the credential's effective expiry, and the host MUST fail closed on `retain_until <= now_unix` (a retention window that has already ended makes reserve-before-act vacuous).
evidence: §3.2 (pinned 9bf7544): '`retain_until` (integer, **REQUIRED**) — Unix seconds until which the host **MUST** retain the consumed nonce.' — no lower bound relative to `now_unix` or expiry.
§3.4 schema (pinned): `"retain_until": { "type": "integer" }` — no minimum at all; `0` and negative values are schema-valid.

§9 registry (pinned): 'expired | proof-anchored `now_unix >= effective_expiry` — a strict comparison; the equality boundary is rejected.' — establishes that the proof is live for all `now_unix < effective_expiry`, i.e. after an early eviction.

§4.1 (pinned): 'a verifier **MUST** additionally require `binding.expiry == credential.expiry`' — expiry is signature-bound (v2), so the only unbound liveness parameter left in the replay path is `retain_until`.
Runnable: `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n 'retain_until'` — every occurrence is a definition; none is a bound.

Previous iteration record: experiment `security-researcher-retain-until-schema-unbounded-relative-to-now-unix` dropped_acceptance with finding 'section-label hunk headers are invalid unified-diff syntax, and the embedded schema fence prematurely closes the diff block' — formatting, not substance.

candidate.title: No host-conformance vector exercises the deny `detail` object — EVC's only channel for step-up hints
candidate.claim: AuthZEN COAZ/AARP (tracked threat card) carry a third 'prerequisite pending' outcome and draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 models step-up/consent as first-class flows. EVC's closed two-outcome verdict and closed 15-code registry mean a verifier wanting to say 'obtainable after consent' can only stuff hints (retry_after, step_up_url) into the OPTIONAL `detail` object under an existing code. That makes `detail` the load-bearing extensibility surface for admission semantics, yet across all 29 vectors in set 0.7.0 none sends a deny that carries `detail` at all. Two host behaviours are therefore unproven: (1) positive control — a schema-valid deny with a nested `detail` object (including adversarial nested keys such as `"verdict":"allow"` or `"consume_nonces":[]` inside detail) MUST be relayed as that deny, neither rejected as schema_invalid nor upgraded; (2) negative — a deny whose `detail` is a non-object (string/array/null) fails the §3.4 schema and MUST fail closed as schema_invalid. A host that never saw a detail-bearing deny can pass 29/29 while either dropping conforming denies or, worse, letting a nested field reach its allow path.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.3: '`detail` (object, **OPTIONAL**) — structured context for logs/debugging. A verifier **SHOULD** echo the originating internal error code here'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 deny schema: `"detail": { "type": "object" }` inside an `"additionalProperties": false` object — a non-object `detail` is a schema failure, an object with arbitrary nested content is valid

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2: the host MUST treat as deny 'a verdict that otherwise fails the §3.4 verdict schema'; §3.5: the host 'MUST NOT upgrade a `deny` to an `allow`' on any advisory field
Conformance vector index (set 0.7.0, 29 host_behavior vectors): the only deny relay control is host-relay-well-behaved-deny (`deny code=expired`); no listed vector description mentions `detail`

candidate.title: EVC admits a capability class, not an action instance; request extension fields are silently unbound
candidate.claim: Every competing pre-action layer decides per tool call with its arguments in scope: OAP (arXiv 2603.20953) 'intercepts tool calls synchronously before execution, evaluates them against a declarative policy'; agentgateway evaluates CEL rules 'against method invocations such as list_tools and call_tools'; Pomerium's mcp_tool criterion gates 'per-tool allow/deny on every request'. EVC's request carries only agent_name/project_key/program/model/granted_capabilities, and the binding v2 signs exactly six fields, none of which is a tool name or an argument digest. Worse, both the envelope and the inner request object are declared additionalProperties: true while no verifier obligation exists to reject or even acknowledge unknown request fields. A host that adds e.g. tool_args_sha256 to request and receives allow has no way to know the verifier never looked at it: extension fields create a fail-open belief without a fail-closed rule. EVC should state that (a) the decision is a capability-class admission unless the action instance is folded into a granted_capabilities token so it is covered by the signed binding, and (b) request extension fields are not authorization inputs unless a verifier's documented contract says so, so hosts MUST NOT assume they were verified.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.2 request schema: `"additionalProperties": true` on the envelope and again on the inner `request` object; no verifier MUST governs unknown request fields anywhere in §2

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.1: `granted_capabilities` are 'host-defined capability tokens the host intends to grant. They are opaque strings that the verifier maps to its internal permission model' — no tool name or argument field exists

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §4.1: 'Let `binding` be the object with exactly the six fields `agent_name`, `project_key`, `program`, `model`, `capabilities` (a string array), and `expiry`' — the signed surface cannot bind an action instance
https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20953 — OAP 'intercepts tool calls synchronously before execution, evaluates them against a declarative policy, and produces a cryptographically signed audit record'
https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/main/mcp/mcp-authz/ — CEL rules evaluated against `call_tools` invocations; hidden-tool calls rejected with an authorization error
https://www.pomerium.com/blog/top-5-agentic-gateways-for-securing-mcp-tool-calls-in-2026 — `mcp_tool` criterion for per-tool allow/deny on every request
candidate.proposed_artifact: A staged prose-only diff (wire unchanged) to §2.1/§2.2 and the -02 draft request section adding a normative 'extension fields are not authorization inputs' rule for hosts and verifiers, plus an informative 'action-instance binding' note showing the capability-token fold so the tool/argument instance lands inside the signed binding.

score.reason: Pinned request schemas accept extension fields without defining their authorization guarantees, supporting a bounded clarification of host assumptions and documented capability-token bindings.

candidate.title: draft-kondoju-evc-01 makes the JSON Schemas normative but has no reference for JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (-02 blocker: unreferenced normative dependency)
candidate.claim: Section 4 states the schemas 'appear normatively' in the schemas appendix, and the fail-closed rule (§4.2, §6) is defined in terms of a verdict 'failing the verdict schema'. Both schemas declare `$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` and rely on 2020-12-specific keyword semantics (`exclusiveMinimum` as a number, `const`, `oneOf`, `additionalProperties:false`). The references section lists only RFC2119/RFC8174/RFC8259 as normative and no JSON Schema document at all, so an IETF reviewer cannot resolve the dependency and idnits will flag it. Resolution: add a normative reference `I-D.bhutton-json-schema` (draft-bhutton-json-schema-01, JSON Schema: A Media Type for Describing JSON Documents) plus `I-D.bhutton-json-schema-validation` for `const`/`exclusiveMinimum`/`minItems`, and add one sentence in §4 stating that where the prose field rules and the schema disagree the prose controls, so the downref to an expired I-D does not carry the whole normative weight. Alternatively demote the schemas to informative transcriptions and restate the closed-enum and additionalProperties rules in prose; the loop should stage the reference-addition form because the host-conformance suite already tests schema-derived behavior.

candidate.title: Timeout kill of the verifier parent leaves the fd-3 worker (and any grandchild) alive: late nonce burn + lingering verification of a denied request
candidate.claim: §7.2 obligates the host to 'kill the process and deny' on timeout, but §5.1 makes the reference verifier a two-process design (parent + worker on fd 3). 'The process' is singular and unqualified: a host that sends SIGKILL to the direct child PID only (the naive spawn/kill idiom in Node, Rust std, Python subprocess) leaves the worker running with the full request in memory. Attack/consequence: in local nonce mode the orphaned worker can finish verification and durably burn the presentation's nullifier AFTER the host has already denied, so the legitimate retry of the same presentation is rejected `nonce_replayed`; an attacker who can induce slow verification (large but under-bound bundle, many Groth16 verifies) turns every timeout into a one-shot burn of the victim agent's nonce. Secondarily, orphaned workers accumulate across timeouts (resource exhaustion) and any grandchild holding the inherited stdout write end can keep the host's read-until-EOF loop open. No vector in set 0.7.0 observes process-tree state after the host's timeout kill (host-deny-no-output-timeout and host-deny-partial-json-timeout only assert the deny/classification).
evidence: §7.2 (pinned 9bf7544): 'timeout (§6) — the host **MUST** kill the process and deny;' — singular 'the process', no mention of the process group, session, or descendants.

§5.1 (pinned 9bf7544): 'the command **spawns a worker** process that performs the entire verification; the worker's stdio binds fd 0 = request in, **fd 1 = captured** ... **fd 3 = the private verdict channel**' — the reference verifier is by construction a parent+worker pair, so a PID-only kill provably leaves the verifier that is actually doing the work running.

Runnable: `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n -i 'process group\|descendant\|orphan\|setsid\|killpg'` returns no matches; `git show 9bf754441ab36ab93992ed5936d34c44a4128f92:spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md | grep -n 'kill the process'` shows the singular obligation.

Vector index (set 0.7.0, 29 vectors) — the two timeout vectors 'host-deny-no-output-timeout' and 'host-deny-partial-json-timeout' assert the verdict outcome only; none describes an assertion over the verifier's process tree after the kill.

Registry §9 (pinned): 'nonce_replayed | the proof's one-time nonce was already seen (local mode)' — the local-mode burn is durable, so a post-deny burn by an orphan is user-visible on the next honest presentation.
